record.reliability_note: The vendor shows a risk score of 8% and 5% for its two samples; no throughput, ban or replacement measurement was made.
record.confidence_note: Prices, terms and the two ISP samples are read from the vendor pages on 2026-11-03 and the ASN holders are measured through RIPE. The sold addresses are masked, so no delivered address was looked up.
record.price_per_tb_month: not applicable: an address, not a byte; from USD 1.80 per IP at the entry price
record.notes: The domain fluxisp.com answers HTTP 301 to https://zooproxy.com/, so the vendor named FluxISP on the forum source is this vendor under its present name. The two ISP samples on the pricing page are masked (64.93.*.205 and 162.141.*.52), so they cannot be looked up as addresses; the ASN holders were measured instead. AS7361 is held by DataZone Networks LLC and is announced; the vendor shows it under Johor Bahru, Malaysia with the type Broadcast ISP, so the registration holder and the shown location differ.

extras.rung_note: The vendor sells registration class explicitly (Native ISP versus Broadcast ISP) and the sample ASNs were checked with RIPE.

record.category: rotating residential and static ISP proxy
record.tier: Residential Proxies (per GB) and Static ISP (per IP)

free_tier.stated: Residential from $0.38/GB and ISP proxy from $1.80/IP on the home page, with 'Start Free Trial' on the sign-up button. The FAQ limits that: 'Some plans include a free trial. You can contact our online support to claim it for free.'
free_tier.notes: The trial size is not stated on any page read: unverified: behind a contact.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: an address or a traffic quota, not an object

retention.stated: not applicable: a proxy session or a rented address, not stored bytes

egress.terms: Residential traffic is billed per GB with larger plans cheaper per GB and custom pricing above 10 TB; static ISP plans are 'priced by IP and rental period, with no additional charges based on traffic usage'.

record.interface_detail: HTTPS, HTTP and SOCKS5; residential sessions are sticky for 1 to 120 minutes or rotate on every request; static ISP plans support HTTP(S) and SOCKS5.
record.tooling: Any client that speaks an HTTP(S) or SOCKS5 proxy with a username and password or an allowlisted source address: curl -x, python requests, rclone --socks5, or a host-side hop for a runtime that cannot dial a proxy itself.
record.chaining: A host-side hop dials the vendor's HTTP(S) or SOCKS5 endpoint with credentials; the upstream sees an address from the vendor's pool in place of the caller's address.

limits.value: Residential from $0.38/GB; contact sales above 10 TB
Unlimited Traffic - Port plan: 6 Mbps per port from $0.38/port/day; Unlimited Traffic - Bandwidth plan from $19.67/day

record.limits_note: Static ISP sample rows on the pricing page show a 'Broadcast ISP' address in Johor Bahru, Malaysia under AS7361 (DataZone Networks LLC) and a 'Native ISP' address in Seoul under AS9848 (Sejong Networks), both labelled 'Home Bandwidth IP' with a 'Risk Score' of 8% and 5%; the addresses are masked, so no registry lookup of an address was possible. A RIPE Stat lookup of the two ASNs gave holders DATAZONE - DataZone Networks LLC (ARIN) and SejongTelecom-AS-KR-KR - SEJONG NETWORKS (APNIC).
record.binding_note: The residential product is metered per GB; the static ISP product is per IP and rental period with no traffic fee.

identity_cost.detail: The sign-up page asks for a password of 8 to 20 characters and an emailed 'Verification code', with a Google sign-in alternative; no phone, card or identity document is on the form. Payment is by card, cryptocurrency, Alipay or bank transfer.

record.reliability_note: https://www.fluxisp.com/ resolves to zooproxy.com, so the FluxISP name now maps to this vendor. The 'Broadcast ISP' sample is registered to a hosting-style AS (DataZone Networks) while its 'IP Category' reads 'Home Bandwidth IP'; the registration class of any live exit was not checked (rung 5).
record.confidence_note: Prices, session rules, sign-up fields and payment methods are from the vendor's pages; the pool and class labels are vendor statements; the two ASN holders are a registry lookup of the vendor's published sample rows.
